items.title: Theorem 11.1 (One exceptional hyperplane).
items.note: All hypotheses written out: F finite convex; unique minimizer x_* ∈ P (P = {aᵀx = b}, a unit); K = {F ≤ F(x_0)} compact; Ω open convex ⊇ K; F μ-strongly convex on Ω (EuclideanStrongConvexOn: F - (μ/2)‖x‖² convex on Ω, Euclidean); P_S g = A(x) for every g ∈ ∂F(x), x ∈ Ω; A Lipschitz on Ω (LipschitzOnWith in the sup norm; equivalent since no constant is specified); F locally C^{1,1} on Ω \ P. Conclusion for every run R with R.x 0 = x_0: F(x_k) → F(x_*), x_k → x_*. The library theorem does not need Ω convex (EuclideanStrongConvexOn already includes convexity of Ω). Non-vacuity: first example at the end of the module (objective (11.20), run from spike_run_exists). Wording point W-c (line 32): the hypothesis "Let K={F≤F(x_0)} be compact" is implied by the unique minimizer of the finite convex F (all sublevels are compact, Localization.sublevel_compact); harmless redundancy, kept in the Lean statement as in the TeX.

The display defines the family F(u,v) = ψ(u,v) + h(v), (u,v) = Fin.cons v u. The claim of the sentence (lines 74-81) is that Theorem 11.1 covers the family: with ψ convex with locally Lipschitz gradient (LocallyC11On univ ψ), h finite convex and locally C^{1,1} off 0, F μ-strongly convex on an open convex neighborhood Ω of the compact sublevel K = {F ≤ F(x_0)}, and the minimizer x_* with v_* = 0, every run from x_0 converges. Uniqueness of the minimizer is derived (unique_of_strong), not assumed. "The relevant neighborhood" is read as an open convex neighborhood of the compact initial sublevel, as in Theorem 11.1.

items.title: Theorem 11.2 (Parallel singular interfaces).

"Every run in K": ∀ k, x_k ∈ K. Conclusion: some cluster point p of (x_k) has 0 ∈ aff ∂F(p). The attained-minimum hypothesis is not needed by the proof. The spike r of (11.18) vanishes for v ≤ 0, so for every v < 0 it has r(v) = 0 > 6v³: the second bound fails at every negative v, hence in every neighbourhood of zero (Lean counterexample spike_cubic_bound_fails). Both bounds hold for every v ≥ 0 and the first for every v (spike_small_bounds; the library's SourceSpikePropertiesTarget states them for v ≥ 0). Nothing in the chapter uses the cubic bound for v < 0. Parallel of the article's M9 (an identity printed without its range).
